localFacts.fact: Iberia allows a cabin bag of max. 56 x 40 x 25 cm and 10 kg; the Summit Carbon II (46 cm), Alpine CF-425 (47 cm) and VEO 3GO (34 cm) fit by length, the Ridgeview (74 cm folded) does not.
In Spain the Primos Trigger Stick Gen3 is sold as a "trípode de caza", adjustable from 61 cm to 157 cm (24 to 62 in).
Spanish retailers list the Leupold Alpine CF-425 from 12,7 cm to 147,3 cm.
MilDot (Spain) presents the Summit Carbon II as made for mountain hunters who need to cut weight without losing stability.

localPainPoints.pain: A cheap, wobbly tripod makes even the best spotting scope useless.
localPainPoints.fix: Pan head instead of ball head, legs wide and low, thickest sections first, pack on the hook in wind.

quotes.text: El mejor telescopio con un trípode de chicle que se mueve sin parar no vale para nada.

localPainPoints.pain: An 80-85 mm scope pushes the whole kit past 4 kg because the tripod has to be heavier too.
localPainPoints.fix: For an 85 mm scope carry the Ridgeview (9,9 kg rating); with a 65 mm scope the 1,13 kg Summit is enough when seated.

quotes.text: seguramente se vaya a los 1,8 - 2 kg de peso, y el trípode tendrá que ser también de más de 2 kg

localPainPoints.pain: Rececho hunters say binoculars above 10x need support, and a spotting scope for judging a trophy needs a tripod.
localPainPoints.fix: For binoculars only, the 970 g VEO 3GO; for a scope, the Summit or Ridgeview with a pan head.

quotes.text: que NO PASEN DE 10 aumentos, sino, hace falta apoyarlos

localGain.point: Which tripods fit an Iberia cabin bag (56 cm) for a hunting trip by plane.
Rececho and alta montaña framing with Spanish hunters' own objections (binoculars above 10x, 80-85 mm scope weight).
Metric figures as sold in Spain (Primos 61-157 cm, Leupold 12,7-147,3 cm).
